To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The quality of key financial data disclosed by exempt proprietary companies is not good; and (2) The annual reporting requirements for exempt proprietary companies are not justified in terms of their contribution to public interest.

(1) the annual reporting requirements for exempt proprietary companies are not in the public's best interests, (2) there are alternative explanations to the protection of the interests of investors for the introduction and maintenance of the requirements, and (3) the key financial data disclosures in the annual returns of exempt proprietary companies are unreliable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of exempt proprietary companies.
whether or not the annual reporting requirements imposed on exempt proprietary companies by the Corporations Law are in the public interest.
the regulation of small business enterprises in the form of annual reporting requirements and the disclosure of key financial data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the annual reporting requirements imposed on small business enterprises should be modified to reduce the burden on business without jeopardising the public interest.
the maintenance of existing reporting requirements for exempt proprietary companies is not in the interests of the public.
the annual reporting requirements are not in the public's interest, and that the key financial data disclosures are not reliable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the public interest is not well-served by the annual reporting requirements for exempt proprietary companies and the ASC should be encouraged to implement the recommendations of the Corporates Law Simplification Task force in this area.

the annual reporting requirements for exempt proprietary companies should be retained for those exempt proprietary companies that are subsidiaries of public companies or that have public debt securities on issue.
annual reporting requirements should be maintained for small business enterprises which are operated as public companies and for small business enterprises operated as private companies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the annual reporting requirements for exempt proprietary companies should be modified.
there are a lot of exemptions for small companies in Australia and that they should be used to reduce the compliance burden for small companies.
there is a need to re‐examine the annual reporting requirements imposed on small business enterprises and the quality of key financial data disclosed.
